title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit
shortDescription: The ECM detected a general circuit fault in the engine oil pressure sensor or switch.
fullDescription:
P0520 indicates the powertrain control module has detected an electrical fault in the engine oil pressure sensor or switch circuit. The ECM uses this signal to monitor lubrication pressure and trigger warnings if pressure drops below safe thresholds.

The fault may be open circuits, shorts, or signal values outside the plausible range. Driving with unverified oil pressure is risky because true low pressure can destroy the engine quickly.
safetyImpact: Oil pressure monitoring is disabled; a real low-oil event may go undetected and cause catastrophic engine damage.

causes.cause: Damaged wiring or connector at sensor

symptoms: No oil pressure reading on gauge

fixSteps.title: Scan codes
fixSteps.instruction: Record freeze frame and related codes.

fixSteps.title: Verify oil level and quality
fixSteps.instruction: Check dipstick; top up or change oil if needed.

fixSteps.title: Measure pressure with mechanical gauge
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm actual oil pressure meets spec before replacing electronics.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Check wiring continuity and sensor resistance/voltage.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap oil pressure sensor and clear codes.

faq.a: Only briefly and only after confirming actual oil pressure is normal with a mechanical gauge.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Oil pressure sensor signal is outside the expected performance range.
fullDescription:
P0521 sets when the oil pressure sensor reports values that are electrically valid but implausible for current engine operating conditions (for example, flat readings across RPM changes, or values that do not match modeled pressure).

Root causes include a failing sensor, clogged sensor port, actual pressure problems, or wiring issues that add resistance to the signal.
safetyImpact: Monitoring accuracy is reduced; unnoticed low pressure could damage the engine.

fixSteps.title: Read live data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare pressure reading to RPM and temperature to spot the implausibility.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor port
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor and check for sludge/debris.

faq.a: Yes, heavy sludge can affect sensor response.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor Low Voltage
shortDescription: Oil pressure sensor input voltage is below the expected minimum.
fullDescription:
P0522 is stored when the ECM sees a voltage on the oil pressure sensor signal line below its calibrated low threshold, often indicating a short to ground or a failed sensor reporting zero pressure when pressure actually exists.

Before assuming a sensor fault, confirm that actual oil pressure is not genuinely low, because a real no-pressure event will also trip this code.
safetyImpact: If pressure is truly low, continued operation will destroy the engine.

causes.cause: Shorted sensor or harness to ground

fixSteps.title: Stop and verify
fixSteps.instruction: Pull over if oil pressure warning is active; check oil level.

fixSteps.title: Mechanical gauge
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm real oil pressure before electrical diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Wiring inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect signal wire for damage or short to ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If actual pressure is normal, replace the sensor.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor High Voltage
shortDescription: Oil pressure sensor signal voltage is above the expected maximum.
fullDescription:
P0523 indicates the PCM is seeing oil pressure sensor signal voltage above the calibrated maximum, commonly caused by an open circuit, broken signal wire, or sensor internal fault.

Because the reading appears pegged high, the PCM cannot trust the signal for diagnostics or warnings.
safetyImpact: Oil warning logic is compromised; unseen low pressure could cause engine damage.

fixSteps.title: Backprobe signal
fixSteps.instruction: Measure signal voltage at sensor, key on.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Check wire from sensor to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if wiring tests good.

faq.q: Can a bad PCM cause this?
faq.a: Rarely; sensor or wiring is the typical cause.

title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
shortDescription: The ECM has determined that actual oil pressure is below the required threshold.
fullDescription:
P0524 is a direct indicator that measured engine oil pressure is below minimum specification. Unlike sensor circuit codes, this reflects the actual pressure value, not a wiring fault.

Low oil pressure can be caused by low oil level, diluted/wrong viscosity oil, worn oil pump, bearing wear, clogged pickup tube, or a stuck pressure relief valve. This condition can rapidly cause catastrophic engine damage.
safetyImpact: Severe; sustained operation may spin bearings or seize the engine.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level
fixSteps.instruction: Top up to spec with correct viscosity.

fixSteps.title: Measure pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use a mechanical gauge at the sensor port.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pump and pickup
fixSteps.instruction: Drop pan if necessary; replace pump or clean pickup.

fixSteps.title: Evaluate bearings
fixSteps.instruction: Check for bearing wear if pump tests good.

title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit
shortDescription: Fault detected in the cruise control servo control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0525 applies to vehicles with an electronic or vacuum cruise control servo. The PCM has detected that the servo control signal is out of expected range, the servo is not responding to commands, or there is an electrical fault in the circuit.

This typically disables cruise control functionality until repaired but does not affect basic drivability.
safetyImpact: Minimal; only cruise control functionality is lost.

fixSteps.title: Test servo circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Measure command signals with scope or DVOM.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault detected in the cooling fan speed sensor circuit.
fullDescription:
P0526 is set when the PCM detects an invalid signal from the cooling fan speed sensor. Many modern vehicles use feedback from the fan to verify it is running at commanded speed and to detect obstructions or failures.

Without valid feedback, the PCM cannot confirm cooling is working and may command default fan operation or limit performance.
safetyImpact: Cooling monitoring is reduced; engine overheating could go undetected in extreme cases.
symptoms: Fan running at high speed constantly

fixSteps.title: Observe fan operation
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fan spins freely and runs at warm temp.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check fan sensor wiring for damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan/sensor assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install new part, as feedback is usually integrated.

faq.a: Unlikely if fan still runs, but monitor temp gauge.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fan speed sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not match commanded operation.
fullDescription:
P0527 is stored when the cooling fan speed sensor signal fails a plausibility check. The PCM commands a fan speed and expects corresponding feedback, but the reported speed does not match expectations over time.

Root causes include a failing sensor, slipping/binding fan, or marginal wiring connections causing signal dropouts.

fixSteps.title: Scan live data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare commanded vs actual fan RPM.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for intermittent drops while flexing wiring.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fan with integrated sensor.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
shortDescription: No signal detected from the cooling fan speed sensor.
fullDescription:
P0528 sets when the PCM fails to receive any pulse or feedback from the fan speed sensor while the fan is commanded on. This typically points to an open circuit, failed sensor, or seized fan motor.

Without feedback, the PCM may force the fan to full speed continuously as a protective measure.
safetyImpact: Possible overheating if fan motor is also dead.
symptoms: Fan always on or always off

fixSteps.title: Verify fan spins
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the fan physically runs when commanded.

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect for bent or pushed-out terminals.

faq.a: Safety default when feedback is lost.

title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (No Change)
shortDescription: Fan speed feedback does not change as expected with commanded speed.
fullDescription:
P0529 is stored when the PCM detects that fan speed feedback is stuck or unchanging despite varying commands. The fan may actually be running, but the feedback signal is frozen.

This usually points to a stuck sensor, mechanical failure in the fan that prevents speed variation, or a firmware logic fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Check for binding or variable speed function.

faq.a: Can degrade AC performance at idle.

title: Fuel Pump Relay Control Circuit Open
shortDescription: Open circuit detected on the fuel pump relay control line.
fullDescription:
P0627 indicates the PCM cannot drive the fuel pump relay because the control circuit is open. The pump will not run, and the engine will either not start or stall.

Causes include a failed relay, broken wire, corroded connector, or an internal PCM driver fault.

fixSteps.title: Check control wire
fixSteps.instruction: Verify PCM is pulling control line low on key-on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fuse block
fixSteps.instruction: Look for damaged relay socket terminals.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring or PCM
fixSteps.instruction: Fix break or replace PCM as last resort.

title: Fuel Pump Relay Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Fuel pump relay control voltage is below threshold.
fullDescription:
P0628 is set when the PCM detects the fuel pump relay control line is shorted to ground or stuck low unexpectedly. The pump may run continuously or exhibit erratic behavior depending on wiring.

This is a safety-relevant fault because continuous pump operation is a fire risk in a crash.
safetyImpact: Potential for pump to run without command; check for continuous pump operation.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect relay
fixSteps.instruction: Pull relay; test control pin for short to ground.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafed wiring shorting to chassis.

fixSteps.title: PCM test
fixSteps.instruction: If circuit is clean, test PCM output.

faq.a: Minor but real if pump runs continuously.

title: Fuel Pump Relay Control Circuit High
shortDescription: Fuel pump relay control voltage is above threshold.
fullDescription:
P0629 is stored when the PCM detects a high voltage on the fuel pump relay control line when it should be low, typically from an open circuit or short to battery.

The pump may fail to run, causing a no-start or stall.
safetyImpact: Engine may not start or may stall.

causes.cause: Short to power on control line

fixSteps.title: Probe control pin
fixSteps.instruction: Check voltage with relay removed, key on.

fixSteps.title: Test continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Verify wire to PCM is intact.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Fix any breaks or shorts identified.

title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible - ECM/PCM
shortDescription: The PCM lacks a valid VIN or the VIN does not match other modules.
fullDescription:
P0630 is set when the PCM has no VIN stored, has an invalid VIN, or the VIN does not match what other modules (BCM, cluster) report. This typically appears after a module replacement or reflash.

The code will persist until the correct VIN is programmed using a dealer or professional scan tool.
safetyImpact: None directly, but emissions readiness and theft system may be affected.

fixSteps.title: Verify replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm whether PCM was recently replaced.

fixSteps.title: Read stored VIN
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to read VIN from PCM.

fixSteps.title: Program VIN
fixSteps.instruction: Write correct VIN with dealer-level tool.

fixSteps.title: Clear codes
fixSteps.instruction: Reset and verify code does not return.

faq.a: Usually yes, but fix to pass inspection.

title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault detected on cylinder 1 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription:
P0671 is a diesel-specific DTC indicating the glow plug controller detected an electrical fault on the cylinder 1 glow plug circuit. This is typically an open (burned-out plug) or a short.

Glow plugs preheat the combustion chamber for cold starts; a failure will cause hard starting and rough running until the engine warms.
safetyImpact: Cold-start reliability reduced; some regions fail emissions due to white smoke.

fixSteps.title: Test plug resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure glow plug resistance; compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace glow plug
fixSteps.instruction: Torque to spec; use anti-seize per manufacturer guidance.

title: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault detected on cylinder 2 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription:
P0672 indicates the glow plug controller detected an electrical fault on the cylinder 2 glow plug circuit. The most common cause is a burned-out plug.

Diagnose by measuring resistance at the plug; a failed plug typically reads open.

title: Cylinder 3 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault detected on cylinder 3 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0673 is set when the glow plug control module detects an electrical fault on cylinder 3. Diagnose like other cylinder glow plug codes.

faq.a: Yes, more glow cycles wear plugs.

title: Cylinder 4 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault detected on cylinder 4 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0674 sets when the glow plug controller detects a fault on cylinder 4. Diagnosis and repair mirror the other cylinder plug codes.

title: Cylinder 5 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 5 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0675 indicates a fault on cylinder 5 glow plug circuit. Typical of inline-5 and V-configuration diesels.

faq.a: Rear cylinders in V engines can be hard to reach.

title: Cylinder 6 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 6 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0676 is stored when a fault is detected on the cylinder 6 glow plug circuit.

title: Cylinder 7 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 7 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0677 is set when the glow plug controller detects a fault on cylinder 7, typical of V8 diesel engines.

title: Cylinder 8 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 8 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0678 indicates a fault on cylinder 8 glow plug circuit, common on V8 diesel engines. Diagnose and repair similarly to other cylinder plug codes.

title: Cylinder 9 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 9 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0679 is applicable to diesel engines with 9 or more cylinders (commercial/industrial applications). Sets when the glow plug controller detects an electrical fault on the ninth circuit.

title: Cylinder 10 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 10 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0680 is used on V10 and larger diesel engines when a glow plug circuit fault is detected on cylinder 10.

faq.a: Often deep in valley; professional recommended.

title: Cylinder 11 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 11 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0681 applies to engines with 11+ cylinders; sets when the glow plug controller detects an electrical fault on cylinder 11.

title: Cylinder 12 Glow Plug Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on cylinder 12 glow plug circuit.
fullDescription: P0682 is used on V12 diesels when the controller detects an electrical fault on cylinder 12.

title: Glow Plug Control Module to PCM Communication Circuit
shortDescription: Communication fault between the glow plug control module and the PCM.
fullDescription:
P0683 sets when the PCM cannot communicate with or receive valid data from the glow plug control module. This may disable the preheat system entirely, causing hard cold starts.

Causes include a failed glow module, wiring, or CAN bus issue.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install and program glow plug control module.

faq.a: Yes, as a workaround in cold climates.

title: Glow Plug Control Module to PCM Communication Range/Performance
shortDescription: Glow plug module communication data is out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0684 indicates communication with the glow plug control module is present but returning implausible data. The PCM may ignore preheat commands or disable the system.

This is often caused by a failing glow module or intermittent CAN communication.

fixSteps.title: Verify module data
fixSteps.instruction: Read live data from glow module.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Install and program replacement if needed.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Engine oil temperature sensor signal is out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0196 sets when the oil temperature sensor signal is electrically valid but implausible for current operating conditions (for example, oil temp lagging coolant warm-up excessively, or stuck flat during drive).

A failing sensor, clogged sensor port with sludge, or wiring contact issues are common causes.
safetyImpact: Oil protection logic may be less accurate, but immediate driving is usually safe.

fixSteps.title: Compare temps
fixSteps.instruction: Check oil temp vs coolant temp trend on scan tool.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
shortDescription: Oil temperature sensor voltage is below minimum.
fullDescription: P0197 sets when signal voltage from the oil temp sensor is below the calibrated minimum, suggesting a short to ground or sensor failure reporting unreasonably low temperature.

faq.a: No, this is a circuit fault.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit High
shortDescription: Oil temperature sensor voltage is above maximum.
fullDescription: P0198 indicates the sensor signal is above the calibrated maximum voltage, typically an open circuit or a failed sensor reporting extreme cold (in NTC sensors, high voltage = cold).
safetyImpact: Minor; adaptive trims may be off.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: Oil temperature sensor signal drops out intermittently.
fullDescription:
P0199 sets when the oil temperature signal intermittently goes out of range, usually from a marginal connector or sensor beginning to fail.

Wiggle testing and data logging are the best diagnostic approaches.

fixSteps.title: Data log
fixSteps.instruction: Record oil temp signal while driving.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Flex harness near sensor while observing data.

title: Bank 2 Intake Camshaft Actuator A Circuit
shortDescription: Fault detected on bank 2 intake VVT actuator A control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0020 is set when the PCM detects an electrical fault on the bank 2 intake variable valve timing (VVT) actuator A control circuit. Bank 2 is the side not containing cylinder 1.

Typical causes are a failed VVT solenoid, wiring issue, or PCM driver fault. Expect reduced performance and fuel economy.

causes.cause: Clogged solenoid screen from dirty oil

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Verify clean connector and intact wires.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid and oil
fixSteps.instruction: Install new solenoid; change oil if overdue.

faq.a: Yes, dirty oil is a common trigger.

title: Bank 2 Intake Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced
shortDescription: Bank 2 intake cam timing is more advanced than the PCM commanded.
fullDescription:
P0021 is stored when the PCM detects that bank 2 intake camshaft timing is more advanced than its commanded position. Root cause is typically a stuck VVT actuator, oil flow problem, or mechanical cam phaser fault.

Driveability will usually suffer and timing chain tensioner issues should be investigated on high-mileage engines.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level/quality
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure clean oil at correct level.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cam phaser
fixSteps.instruction: Check for wear on phaser and chain.

title: Bank 2 Intake Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded
shortDescription: Bank 2 intake cam timing is more retarded than commanded.
fullDescription:
P0022 sets when bank 2 intake cam timing is measured to be more retarded than commanded. Often caused by a VVT solenoid stuck in a retard position, weak oil pressure, or phaser wear.

Expect reduced low-end torque and possible rough idle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect phaser
fixSteps.instruction: Check phaser for wear or damage.

title: Bank 2 Exhaust Camshaft Actuator B Circuit
shortDescription: Fault on bank 2 exhaust VVT actuator B control circuit.
fullDescription: P0023 is set when the PCM detects an electrical fault on the bank 2 exhaust VVT actuator B control circuit. Causes include a failed exhaust VVT solenoid, wiring fault, or PCM driver fault.

title: Bank 2 Exhaust Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced
shortDescription: Bank 2 exhaust cam timing is more advanced than commanded.
fullDescription:
P0024 sets when bank 2 exhaust VVT timing is more advanced than the PCM commanded. Often caused by a stuck exhaust VVT phaser or solenoid.

Results in reduced efficiency and possible DTC-related driveability issues.

faq.a: Long-term timing issues can harm cats.

title: Bank 2 Exhaust Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded
shortDescription: Bank 2 exhaust cam timing is more retarded than commanded.
fullDescription: P0025 indicates that bank 2 exhaust camshaft timing is more retarded than the commanded position. Often caused by stuck solenoid, low oil pressure, or phaser wear.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
shortDescription: Bank 1 intake valve control solenoid performance is out of range.
fullDescription:
P0026 sets when the intake valve control solenoid on bank 1 does not respond mechanically as expected. Typically caused by a sticking solenoid, clogged oil passage, or electrical fault.

Result is poor VVT response, rough idle, and reduced efficiency.

fixSteps.title: Clean solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean with solvent; replace filter screen.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Install new solenoid if cleaning fails.

faq.a: Clean first; replace if code returns.

title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
shortDescription: Bank 1 exhaust valve control solenoid performance is out of range.
fullDescription:
P0027 indicates the bank 1 exhaust valve control solenoid is not performing within expected range. Usually caused by contamination or solenoid wear.

Resolution parallels P0026 but on the exhaust side.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
shortDescription: Bank 2 intake valve control solenoid performance is out of range.
fullDescription: P0028 mirrors P0026 but on bank 2. The intake valve control solenoid is failing to operate within expected range.

title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
shortDescription: Bank 2 exhaust valve control solenoid performance is out of range.
fullDescription: P0029 sets when the bank 2 exhaust valve control solenoid performance is out of range. Mirrors P0027 on bank 2.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: CVT transmission fluid pressure sensor A is out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0841 (v2, CVT-specific application) sets when the transmission fluid pressure sensor A reports values outside of expected operating range for the CVT. Causes include low fluid, failing pump, sticky valve body, or sensor fault.

Continued driving with low line pressure can damage belts and pulleys.

fixSteps.title: Check fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Verify CVT fluid level and condition.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/pump
fixSteps.instruction: If fluid and valve body are good.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
shortDescription: Electrical fault on transmission fluid pressure sensor B circuit.
fullDescription:
P0845 sets when the PCM/TCM detects an electrical fault on the transmission fluid pressure sensor B circuit. Sensor B typically reads secondary pulley or clutch apply pressure in CVT applications.

Causes include sensor failure, wiring fault, or connector corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for damage or corrosion at sensor B.

faq.a: Common on CVT but applies to many transmissions.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Transmission fluid pressure sensor B is out of expected range.
fullDescription: P0846 sets when sensor B signal is electrically valid but does not match commanded or modeled pressure. Typical causes include failing sensor, clogged port, or low pressure.
safetyImpact: Potential CVT damage if pressure actually low.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if actual pressure normal.

faq.a: Depends on root cause; verify actual pressure.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Transmission fluid pressure sensor B voltage below minimum.
fullDescription: P0847 indicates sensor B voltage is below threshold, suggesting a short to ground, failed sensor, or true low pressure condition.
safetyImpact: CVT may be at risk if real pressure is low.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
shortDescription: Transmission fluid pressure sensor B voltage above maximum.
fullDescription: P0848 sets when sensor B signal is above threshold, indicating an open circuit, disconnected sensor, or sensor fault.
